hook: Tim Dettmers built his career on the wager that making large models run on far less hardware would open up who gets to do AI research at all. His PhD work at the University of Washington, advised by Luke Zettlemoyer, produced LLM.int8() in 2022 and then QLoRA in 2023, a method that let a 65 billion parameter language model be fine-tuned on a single 48 gigabyte GPU. He maintains bitsandbytes, the open-source quantization library those methods run on, and in 2024 he became an Assistant Professor at Carnegie Mellon University while continuing as a Research Scientist at the Allen Institute for AI. His own faculty page describes his focus as making foundation models accessible to researchers and practitioners by reducing their resource requirements.
name: Tim Dettmers

quote.text: I believe open source can be competitive and might be actually just overtake the closed source APIs because of flexibility, because of ecosystem.
quote.context: From an interview with Tim Dettmers on the Interconnects newsletter and podcast about open-source AI

timeline.event: Publishes LLM.int8(), an 8-bit inference method for large language models, in August
timeline.impact: Makes it possible to run billion-parameter models on less hardware without losing accuracy

timeline.event: Publishes QLoRA in May with co-authors Artidoro Pagnoni, Ari Holtzman, and Luke Zettlemoyer
timeline.impact: Cuts the hardware needed to fine-tune large language models by combining 4-bit quantization with low-rank adapters

timeline.event: Receives the PyTorch Foundation Award and the Google Open Source Award
timeline.impact: Recognizes the reach of the bitsandbytes library across the open-source AI ecosystem

timeline.event: Named an AI2050 Early Career Fellow and joins Carnegie Mellon University as an Assistant Professor
timeline.impact: Moves his research on efficient AI methods into a faculty role

timeline.event: Receives the Google ML and Systems Junior Faculty Award
timeline.impact: Continued recognition for his systems-focused machine learning research

quick_facts: Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Machine Learning at Carnegie Mellon University since 2024
Also a Research Scientist at the Allen Institute for AI
PhD from the University of Washington, advised by Luke Zettlemoyer
Lead author of QLoRA (2023) and LLM.int8() (2022), efficient quantization and fine-tuning methods for large language models
Creator and maintainer of the open-source bitsandbytes library, which his CMU faculty page lists at 2.2 million monthly installations
Received the 2023 PyTorch Foundation Award and the 2023 Google Open Source Award, and was named a 2024 AI2050 Early Career Fellow

achievements.title: QLoRA
achievements.impact: Co-authored the May 2023 paper introducing 4-bit quantized fine-tuning with low-rank adapters, which the paper reports let a 65-billion-parameter model be fine-tuned on a single 48GB GPU while matching full 16-bit fine-tuning performance.

achievements.title: LLM.int8()
achievements.impact: Published the August 2022 paper introducing an 8-bit matrix multiplication method that let large language models run inference at scale without the performance loss earlier quantization approaches caused.

achievements.title: bitsandbytes
achievements.impact: Created and maintains the open-source library implementing these quantization methods, reaching 2.2 million monthly installations according to his CMU faculty page.

achievements.title: Assistant Professor, Carnegie Mellon University
achievements.impact: Joined CMU's Computer Science and Machine Learning Departments in 2024 to continue research on computationally efficient deep learning methods and open-source agent systems.
